back: Addictive; raises heart rate and blood pressure; narrows blood vessels; makes blood clot more easily.
Contains carcinogens (lung cancer); coats the airways, damages cilia and causes extra mucus.
Combines with haemoglobin, so the blood carries less oxygen.
notes: Not the same as carbon dioxide.

back: A substance that can cause cancer.

front: Short-term effects of smoking on the airways?
back: Cilia damaged and stop beating; extra mucus; coughing; less oxygen carried; raised heart rate.
Long-term inflammation of the bronchi, blocked with mucus: persistent cough and repeated chest infections.
Breakdown of the walls of the alveoli, giving a much smaller surface area for gas exchange; causes severe breathlessness.

front: How does smoking cause lung cancer?
back: Carcinogens in tar damage the genes of cells, which divide out of control and form a tumour.
Breathing in other people's tobacco smoke; it raises the risk of lung and heart disease in non-smokers.
Less oxygen reaches the fetus (carbon monoxide, nicotine), so babies tend to have a lower birth mass.
